title: Listing Partner Onboarding Bridge — checklist + creative prompts (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a pragmatic, sprint-friendly checklist + micro-copy prompt bank for onboarding partners into cloud marketplaces (AWS/Azure/GCP). It's intended for the launch sprint (partner-integrations lane) and should sit ahead of the final marketplace acceptance playbook. Focus: fast, low-friction listing that meets technical, legal, and creative gates with minimal back-and-forth.

Background / context:
- Problem: Partner listings stall because teams submit incomplete telemetry/entitlement info and unclear copy. Our intake needs to be prescriptive.
- Goal: reduce partner turnaround time from intake -> publish from avg 12 days to <= 4 days for standard integrations.
- Audience: partner PMs/engineers, GTM launch owners, catalog publishers.
- This doc is an iteration on existing marketplace checklists (see CONF-2319) but framed as a "bridge" — short, prioritized items + ready-to-use copy snippets.

How to use this doc:
- Follow the "Must-have" checklist during intake. Items marked "Nice-to-have" can be staged as follow-up tasks post-publish.
- Copy snippets below are intentionally terse — use them verbatim for landing tiles, then expand in the partner page.
- Assign an owner for each acceptance gate in the intake form (Partner PM, Solutions Engineer, Security reviewer).

MUST-HAVE acceptance gates (blocking for publish):
1) Technical contract & entitlement
   - Confirm SKU mapping and billing model (trial SKU? metered? subscription?) --> fill field: SKU_ID, Billing_Type.
   - Partner provides integration docs link + sample request/response (API keys scrubbed).
   - Verify deployment compatibility: hosted API or private (VPC) option; if private, attach network diagram.
   - PR: GO-7890 must be linked for infra changes.

2) Security & Privacy
   - Data residency requirement declared (yes/no + region).
   - Minimal security attestation: SOC2 or equivalent; if not available, complete the short security questionnaire (doc template attached in CONF-2319).
   - KMS/HSM usage called out for private deployments (required for enterprise).

3) Telemetry & observability
   - Provide readiness for basic telemetry hooks (success/error counts, latencies) via our telemetry contract.
   - Confirm opt-in flags for debug logs and ensure PII excluded.

4) Creative + copy sanity check (tile + short description) — tile copy must be <= 110 characters; description <= 600 characters.
   - Provide 1 line hero (tile) + 2–3 sentence description + 3 bullets of key value props.

5) Legal & Terms
   - Licensing model agreed: BYOM, Redwood-hosted, or co-hosted.
   - Reviewed by Legal (Y/N) with date.

6) QA smoke test evidence
   - Provide runbook for vendor smoke test and screenshot evidence for the happy-path flow.
   - Attach test accounts (or notes for how to provision trial).

NICE-TO-HAVE (post-publish staging allowed):
- Localization strings for en/fr/de/es (basic).
- Advanced telemetry (per-route latency histograms).
- Marketing assets: 1–2 customer quotes, 16:9 hero image (1920x1080).
- Implementation guide video (2–3 min).

Priority checklist (intake sequence):
- Day 0: Partner fills intake form (fields: contact, SKU, short tile, one-paragraph description, billing model).
- Day 0–1: GTM reviewer checks MUST-HAVE gates; security reviews.
- Day 1–2: Engineering validates integration + QA smoke run.
- Day 2–3: Legal signs off, assets wired to publisher.
- Day 3–4: Catalog publish (internal QA) -> Go-live.

Quick copy prompt bank (use these verbatim for catalog tiles and hero blurbs):
- Tile (110 char max): "Low-latency LLM inference with flexible hosting: Redwood + PartnerName"
- Short description (<= 600 chars): "Integrate PartnerName with Redwood Inference to run LLM workloads with predictable latency and cost controls. Choose hosted, dedicated, or private deployment; get built-in observability, billing integration, and enterprise-grade security. Start a free trial or contact sales for dedicated capacity."
- 3 bullets (for catalog UX):
  * "Fast inference: Serving runtime optimized for GPU throughput and low tail latency."
  * "Flexible deployment: Hosted API, reserved dedicated pools, or private VPC/on-prem."
  * "Cost controls: batching, KV caching, and quantization recommendations to reduce per-token cost."

Alternate short hero variants (use as A/B test):
- "Ship LLM features fast — Redwood + PartnerName, hosted or private."
- "Predictable latency, lower cost — production-ready inference with PartnerName and Redwood."

Technical dependencies checklist (engineering):
- API compatibility: verify OpenAPI spec or equivalent. Acceptable auth: API key or OAuth2 (document).
- Model packaging: if partner supplies custom model, confirm model format (ggml, ONNX, torchscript) and quantization level.
- Resource footprint: submit expected RPS, p50/p95 latency targets, and average prompt lengths.
- Fallback plan: specify fallback model variant for capacity constraints.

Telemetry & monitoring contract (minimal fields to provide):
- metric names: partner.request.count, partner.request.latency_p95, partner.request.errors
- tracing sample rate: default 1% (adjustable)
- logs: redacted request IDs only.

Publisher ops steps (for catalog team):
- Validate tile copy length and alt-text for images.
- Map SKU_ID to internal billing SKU and confirm entitlements in billing dashboard.
- Add partner contact + support SLAs to the listing metadata.

Common failure modes and mitigations:
- Missing SKU mapping -> block publish: fix by billing ops (owner: finance ops).
- Private deploy network blind spots -> require network diagram and SRE signoff.
- Copy lacks security claims -> vendor-edit to remove unverified claims and re-submit.

Open questions / known risks (to resolve during intake):
- Does the partner expect metered billing across multiple cloud regions? (affects billing SKU).
- For private deployments, are they expecting cross-account infra provisioning? Need cloud-owner conversation.
- Does the partner require audit log exports to a third-party SIEM? If yes, legal + security become longer lead.

Owner & responsibilities (suggested):
- Catalog owner (GTM): Ava Chen — intake owner, copy sanity.
- Solutions Eng: Diego Ramirez — integration validation and smoke test.
- Security reviewer: Priya Nair — run security questionnaire.
- Billing owner: Liam O'Connor — SKU mapping and entitlements.

Proposed intake form fields (minimum):
- Partner name (string), Contact email, SKU_ID, Billing model (dropdown), Short tile, Short description, Regions, Security attestation (Y/N + doc link), Test account details, Integration docs URL.

Example snack-case checklist to paste into Jira acceptance criteria:
- "GIVEN partner submitted intake with SKU_ID and tile
  WHEN GTM validates gates AND engineering runs smoke test
  THEN listing can be published to dev-catalog and scheduled for prod rollout."

Next steps (this doc):
- Merge final acceptance fields into the intake form (GO-7890).
- Ship a lightweight intake template to partners (editable doc).
- Run one pilot onboarding with BetaPartnerCo to validate the 4-day SLA.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Add sample image spec and alt-text checklist.
- Draft a short partner-facing email template for "what we need to publish you".
- Coordinate with legal to produce a one-click checklist for standard terms.

Links & refs:
- Confluence: CONF-2319 (catalog onboarding foundation)
- Jira: GO-7890 (intake form and automation)
- GitHub: marketplace-integration PR #142 (billing SKU support)

-- end of draft --

Raw change log:
